headline: Medium risk: cognee can ingest sensitive support data while spring-integration-samples is network-isolated, creating default-path leakage and workflow-cascade concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can process documents and support data, so if B’s outputs are manually copied into A or routed through a shared workspace, prompt-like content could influence A. B has no documented output channel or shared channel, so the pathway is not default and remains limited. Uncertainty about undocumented bridges pushes this above none.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected by manual copy-paste or a shared file drop
IF B’s generated text is later ingested by A as trusted document content
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted agent output into A
Use a separate staging folder for B outputs
Add a human review step before A ingests any B-generated text

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches personal data, finance data, and support history, but B has no data classes touched and no network egress. There is no documented shared workspace or upload path, so direct leakage from A to B is not evidenced. The pair still warrants low severity because A’s sensitive inputs could be exposed if an undocumented bridge exists.
conditions: IF A and B are placed in the same shared filesystem
IF B is extended to read files produced by A
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Restrict file permissions on A outputs
Do not mount A’s data directory into B

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has allowlisted network egress and session-scoped memory; B has no documented write, network, or mutable-resource capabilities. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource in the profiles, a capability conflict is not plausible from the documented pair.
conditions: IF B is later given write access to the same directory or service as A
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Document any future shared resource before enabling it

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces decisions, workflows, and expert SQL queries, which B could treat as authoritative if its integration pipeline consumes A’s outputs without verification. B’s profile does not show validation or critical review controls, so a mistaken A output could cascade into downstream planning or actions. This is an inferred interaction, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text as authoritative input
IF no verification or cross-check step is inserted between A and B
mitigations: Insert a validation step between A and B
Require source citations for A outputs before B uses them
Have a human review any A-derived recommendation before action

E_compliance.rationale: A explicitly touches personal data, finance data, customer support data, and support history, while B’s profile gives no residency, retention, or certification controls. Because the pair’s compliance posture is undocumented, any cross-system handling of regulated data could create a mismatch; uncertainty escalates above low. B is not cited for a specific violation because its compliance fields are absent.
conditions: IF regulated data from A is exported into B or a downstream system
IF B is deployed under a different retention or residency policy than A
mitigations: Classify A data before any transfer
Block regulated data from entering B until policies are confirmed
Record retention and residency settings for both systems
